appearance_description: Set the StackFerry color scheme. This setting applies only to this application.
theme_system_description: Follow the operating system light or dark appearance.
language_system_description: Follow the operating system language setting.
mica_description: Apply system Mica to the sidebar background. Available on Windows 11 22H2 and later.
mica_enabled_description: The sidebar uses system Mica sampled from the desktop wallpaper.
mica_unsupported_description: Mica is not supported on this system. Windows 11 22H2 or later is required.
routing_description: When the routing queue is not empty, that CLI sends requests through a local 127.0.0.1 proxy and attempts upstreams in queue order. The currently enabled custom provider is placed first and participates in circuit breaking. Official login is never added to the queue.
routing_description_codex: When the Codex queue is not empty, Codex sends requests through a local 127.0.0.1 proxy and attempts upstreams in queue order. The currently enabled custom provider is placed first and participates in circuit breaking. Official login is never added to the queue.
routing_description_claude: When the Claude queue is not empty, Claude Code and Desktop send requests through a local 127.0.0.1 proxy and attempt upstreams in queue order. The currently enabled custom provider is placed first and participates in circuit breaking. Official login is never added to the queue.
routing_description_grok: When the Grok queue is not empty, Grok Build sends requests through a local 127.0.0.1 proxy and attempts upstreams in queue order. The currently enabled custom provider is placed first and participates in circuit breaking. Official login is never added to the queue.
routing_active_description: The CLI currently points to the local proxy. Quitting StackFerry restores a direct upstream.
routing_active_description_codex: config.toml currently points to the local proxy. Quitting StackFerry restores a direct upstream.
routing_active_description_claude: Claude settings currently point to the local proxy. Quitting StackFerry restores a direct upstream.
routing_active_description_grok: config.toml currently points to the local proxy. Quitting StackFerry restores a direct upstream.
routing_inactive_description: The queue is empty, or official login is enabled. Enabling a custom provider with a non-empty queue switches to failover routing automatically.
routing_breaker_description: These limits apply to every CLI lane. Breaker state is still tracked separately per lane.
routing_queue_description: Queue order is the upstream attempt order. The enabled provider appears in the queue and participates in circuit breaking. Drag the handle to reorder. An open breaker can be restored immediately.
routing_queue_empty: No providers are in the queue. Choose “Add to queue” from a provider menu.
routing_failure_threshold_description: After this many consecutive failures, the breaker opens and that upstream is skipped for the remainder of the round.
routing_recovery_wait_description: After the breaker opens, wait this many seconds before sending one half-open probe.
routing_half_open_description: The breaker closes after this many consecutive successful half-open probes.
routing_logs_caption: Only request metadata is retained. Request bodies and API keys are not stored.
routing_queue_join_hint: If the current upstream fails, this provider is attempted next in queue order.
routing_queue_leave_hint: This provider is at position {position} in the failover queue. Select again to remove it.
routing_queued_cannot_enable: Queued providers cannot be enabled from the list. Remove it first, or drag it to the front in routing settings.
restart_codex_description: The configuration has been written. Restart Codex or the terminal for the change to take effect.
about_description: Manage provider configuration for Codex and other CLIs, and write it to local configuration files.
providers_empty_description: Add a provider, or switch to official login.
field_wire_api_responses_description: The upstream uses the Responses protocol. Requests are forwarded unchanged.
field_wire_api_chat_description: The upstream uses Chat Completions. The local proxy translates requests to Responses.
api_key_keep_placeholder: Leave blank to keep the current key
session_catalog_description: Skip this unless you want to replace Codex’s /model list. Leave empty to keep the built-in catalog.
session_catalog_placeholder: Leave empty for the built-in list
session_model_description: Maps to the top-level model field in config.toml. Written when a provider is enabled, or when the currently enabled provider is saved. After restarting Codex, it is used as the startup model. If a catalog is set, the default must come from that list.
session_reasoning_hint_default: Use the model default effort and leave the field unset.
session_reasoning_hint_none: Disable reasoning and prioritize the fastest response.
session_reasoning_hint_minimal: Lowest reasoning intensity. Best for simple, well-scoped tasks.
session_reasoning_hint_low: Light reasoning. Best for small, clearly bounded changes.
session_reasoning_hint_medium: Balances speed and depth for everyday development work.
session_reasoning_hint_high: Increases reasoning depth for complex problems and multi-step changes.
session_reasoning_hint_xhigh: Further increases reasoning depth for high-risk or highly uncertain work.
session_reasoning_hint_max: Uses the highest reasoning intensity for the most difficult problems.
session_reasoning_hint_ultra: Highest reasoning intensity, with possible task delegation.
session_reasoning_hint_persistent: Keeps high reasoning intensity across a long session.
session_reasoning_description: Maps to model_reasoning_effort in config.toml and applies only to the Responses API. max / ultra consume additional quota. Selecting Default leaves the field unset.
session_context_placeholder: e.g. 272000, leave blank for the model default
session_context_description: Maps to model_context_window. The unit is tokens.
session_compact_placeholder: Filled at 90% of the context window
session_compact_description: Maps to model_auto_compact_token_limit. After the context window is set, this value is filled at 90% of that window (the Codex hard cap). It can be changed manually; a later context-window change does not overwrite a custom value.
delete_enabled_description: “{name}” is the currently enabled provider. Deleting it will not automatically switch back to the official configuration. Delete this provider?
delete_description: Delete “{name}”? This removes the configuration from StackFerry only.
claude_empty_description: Add a gateway, or switch to official login.
grok_empty_description: Add a custom model endpoint, or switch to official login.
grok_field_model_description: Sent as the model id in ~/.grok/config.toml. Fetch the list from the provider when the endpoint supports /v1/models.
grok_field_image_description: Optional. The provider must expose OpenAI-compatible /v1/images/generations and /v1/videos/generations. When set, StackFerry writes Grok Build Imagine settings; leave both models empty to leave media unchanged.
grok_field_image_model_hint: Shares the model list fetched by Default model above, or type an id directly. Written to features.image_gen_model_override.
grok_field_image_models_empty: Fetch models from Default model above, or type a model id
grok_field_video_model_hint: Enables video_gen against the media Base URL below. Grok currently sends grok-imagine-video-1.5; the upstream must accept that id.
grok_field_image_base_url_hint: Shared by image and video. Written directly to endpoints.xai_api_base_url. Leave empty to reuse the chat Base URL above.
grok_field_image_base_url_placeholder: Defaults to the Base URL above
grok_field_image_api_key_hint: Shared by image and video auth. Leave empty to reuse the API key above.
grok_field_image_api_key_placeholder: Defaults to the API key above
grok_backend_responses_description: Grok Build calls /v1/responses. Use this for xAI and OpenAI-compatible Responses APIs.
grok_backend_chat_description: Grok Build still talks to StackFerry over /v1/responses; the proxy translates to /v1/chat/completions for this upstream.
grok_session_effort_description: Writes reasoning_effort into the config.toml overlay, then onto the StackFerry model table and models.default_reasoning_effort. Also marks the model as supporting effort. Grok persists none / low / medium / high / xhigh / max. Selecting Default leaves these fields unset.
grok_session_context_placeholder: e.g. 200000, leave blank for the model default
grok_session_context_description: Writes context_window into the overlay, then onto the model table. Grok uses this token count to time auto-compaction. Leave blank to keep Grok’s default for unknown model IDs (200000).
grok_session_compact_description: Writes auto_compact_threshold_percent into the overlay, then onto the model table (0–100). Leave blank to keep Grok’s default. This is a percent of the context window, not a token count.
grok_field_overlay_description: This fragment is merged into ~/.grok/config.toml. The form fields above edit name, model, base_url, api_backend, reasoning_effort, context_window, auto_compact_threshold_percent, and [ui].permission_mode here. [models], [ui], and [permission] merge at the root; other keys merge into this provider’s [model.*] table. api_key, models.default, auxiliary model pins, and ui.fork_secondary_model are written after the overlay and take precedence. Leave empty to append nothing.
toast_grok_enabled: Enabled “{name}”. Restart Grok Build for it to take effect.
claude_hint_description: Enabling a provider also writes the same configuration to Claude Desktop. Fully quit and reopen Desktop for the change to take effect.
claude_field_model_description: Optional. Written as ANTHROPIC_MODEL for Claude Code. Leave the catalog empty so Desktop 3P keeps gateway discovery instead of a one-item inferenceModels pin.
claude_field_models_description: Skip this unless you want to replace Claude Desktop 3P’s picker. Leave empty so Desktop and Claude Code discover models from the gateway /v1/models list.
claude_session_effort_description: Maps to effortLevel in ~/.claude/settings.json. Claude Code persists only low / medium / high / xhigh. Selecting Default leaves the field unset. max applies to the current session only and is not written.
claude_session_context_placeholder: e.g. 200000, leave blank for the model default
claude_session_context_description: Written as the CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS environment variable so Claude Code uses this window for unrecognized gateway model IDs. Values of 1000000 or greater also enable supports1m and prefer1m for Claude Desktop 3P.
claude_session_compact_placeholder: 100000–1000000; filled at 90% of the context window when in range
claude_session_compact_description: Maps to autoCompactWindow in settings.json (100000–1000000 tokens). After the context window is set, this value is filled at 90% of that window when the result is in range. It can be changed manually; a later context-window change does not overwrite a custom value.
claude_session_permission_description: Maps to permissions.defaultMode in ~/.claude/settings.json. Claude Code uses default, acceptEdits, plan, auto, dontAsk, or bypassPermissions. Selecting Default leaves the field unset.
claude_field_overlay_description: Additional JSON is merged into ~/.claude/settings.json. Gateway environment variables, effortLevel, permissions.defaultMode, autoCompactWindow, and CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS are written after this overlay and take precedence. Leave empty to append nothing.
claude_auth_bearer_description: Uses Authorization: Bearer. Maps to ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN.
claude_auth_x_api_key_description: Uses the x-api-key header. Maps to ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
toast_claude_enabled: Enabled “{name}”. Restart Claude Code, and fully quit Claude Desktop 3P, for it to take effect.
toast_enabled_description: Enabled “{name}”. Restart Codex or the terminal for the change to take effect.
toast_enabled_routed: Enabled “{name}”. Failover routing switched to this upstream; no restart is required.

field_toml_description: This fragment is merged into ~/.codex/config.toml. The session fields above edit model, model_reasoning_effort, model_context_window, model_auto_compact_token_limit, and approval_policy here. The custom provider is the [model_providers.<id>] table. name, experimental_bearer_token, and model_provider are written after the overlay and take precedence.

onboarding_welcome_body:
StackFerry sits beside Codex, Claude Code, and Grok. It does not replace those CLIs.

The next steps follow the real path: add and enable providers, sync Skills / MCP, then optional failover. You can skip anytime and replay later from Settings → About.
onboarding_cli_body:
Codex, Claude, and Grok each keep a separate provider list.

Select the CLI you actually use, then add or enable an upstream. Restart that CLI or terminal after enabling so the new config is picked up.
onboarding_add_body:
Add a custom gateway here (address and API key). Official login can stay as-is.

Adding only stores it. Enable writes that CLI's local config after a backup. Relay sites can also send a stackferry:// import link; the app confirms first and never auto-enables.
onboarding_skills_body:
Import reads SKILL.md from a local folder. Market installs from GitHub repos.

StackFerry keeps a copy, then projects it onto the Claude / Codex / Grok targets you select. You do not install the same skill in each CLI separately.
onboarding_mcp_body:
Add a stdio or HTTP MCP server here, or import definitions already on a CLI.

Enable per CLI to apply them to Claude, Codex, and/or Grok. Import skips servers that already exist in StackFerry.
onboarding_settings_body:
Appearance, language, local CLI installs, failover routing, and About live here.

Closing the window hides to the tray and keeps routing running. Quit restores CLI configs from the loopback proxy back to direct upstreams.
onboarding_cli_tools_body:
Detect, install, update, or uninstall local Codex, Claude Code, and Grok Build here.

Uninstalling a CLI does not delete providers saved in StackFerry. Enabling a provider still writes config even if the CLI is missing; you just cannot run it yet.
onboarding_routing_body:
Each CLI has one queue. When the queue is not empty, requests go through 127.0.0.1, try upstreams in order, and use circuit breaking.

Choose Add to failover queue on a provider. The enabled custom provider stays first; official login never joins. Quitting StackFerry restores direct upstreams.
onboarding_about_body:
Replay this walkthrough from here.

If you used cc-switch before, import Codex / Claude providers further down this page. Built-in entries, missing credentials, and names that already exist are skipped. Imported API keys stay valid only on the original device.
onboarding_replay_description: Play the first-launch walkthrough again. It covers providers, Skills, MCP, and failover.
